# Security policy

## Supported versions

Fixes are released for the latest version only; older versions get no backports. Upgrade before you report: the problem may be fixed already.

| Version | Supported |
|---|---|
| `1.3` | yes |
| older | no |

## Reporting a vulnerability

Report it privately through GitHub: [Report a vulnerability](https://github.com/nanolaba/nanolog/security/advisories/new) (the Security tab of the repository). Never in a public issue, pull request or discussion: a vulnerability made public before its fix puts every user at risk.

Include the version, the JDK, what an attacker can do, and the smallest code that shows it. English or Russian.

## What happens next

1. The report is acknowledged in the advisory, before any other work on the project.
2. The problem is reproduced and fixed in a private fork of the advisory, and a release carries the fix.
3. The advisory is published with the release, crediting the reporter unless they prefer otherwise.

## In scope

Nanolog has no network code and no dependencies. What matters is what reaches the log: a secret written despite `LOG.secret` or `nanolog.redact`, a payload of `LOG.content` written in full without `nanolog.content=show`, or a value that forges a line of its own in a `[NANOLOG]` diagnostic or a JSON line.
